gap: No result ChatGPT got states which solar panels each plug-in microinverter can take: the APsystems EZ1-LV accepts 18 A per input across two inputs (25 A short-circuit) with a 27–45 V tracking range and recommended 315–660+ Wp modules, while each Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV takes one module at 14–16 A and 64 V max, so a large modern panel above 14 A fits the EZ1-LV but is current-limited on the smaller HiFlow models.
standout_why: I compared against solarwaypoint.com/best-plug-in-solar-systems (cited), balconysolarkits.us/kits (cited) and pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited). Each one names output VA, certifications and circuit conditions. pluginsolarcheck and Solar Waypoint already give the EZ1-LV's dedicated 10 A circuit or Class A GFCI condition and its locking PIPV plug. balconysolarkits.us and pluginsolarcheck both say outright that they do not list panel Voc, Isc or input current. None of the three gives a panel-to-inverter pairing limit (input voltage, input current, module wattage range, panels per unit) for any inverter.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's EZ1-LV pick for a two-panel build. It is the only candidate with two 18 A inputs and a published 315–660+ Wp module range, so one unit can run two current large-format panels. The HiFlow Pro LV is one panel per unit, and the model has to match the panel: the 360/391/420 models allow 14 A, the 450 allows 15 A and the 500 allows 16 A. A shopper pairing a high-current panel with the $149 HMS-360 would lose output. Panels must stay under the 60–64 V input ceiling. That rules out series-wiring two panels into one input, and it rules out high-voltage rooftop strings.

findings.note: Maker's US page: 'Connect one or two solar panels to a single EZ1'. It also says 'Low-voltage DC design—under 60V'.

findings.label: Max input current per channel
findings.value: 18 A per input, 2 independent MPPT inputs

findings.note: The maker's datasheet and manual links redirect to apsystems.filecloudonline.com, which failed with a self-signed certificate error. Figure taken from the named trade publication.

findings.label: MPPT voltage range
findings.note: Quoted: 'between 27 V and 45 V'. The maker's page gives the DC ceiling only as 'under 60V'.

findings.label: Recommended PV module power
findings.note: Quoted: 'recommended PV module power ratings ranging from 315 Wp to upwards of 660 Wp'.

findings.label: Units per branch circuit
findings.value: Up to 2 EZ1-LV units on one branch circuit; up to 2 registered per system in the app
findings.note: The app limit comes from the maker's page https://usa.apsystems.com/ez1-consumers/ : 'You can register up to two EZ1 microinverters per system.' The CSA conditions (dedicated 10 A circuit or bidirectional Class A GFCI) are already on the rival pages.

findings.label: Price and paired accessories (maker's US store)

findings.note: A 5 m power cord is included. Free shipping covers the lower 48 states only, and orders are limited to 5 units. The page showed no stock status in the read.

findings.note: The maker's US page says 64 V. Retailer solar-electric.com lists 60 V for the HMS-360. The maker's figure is used here.
